name: HiDream-I1 (Full, Dev, Fast)
purpose: Open 17B text-to-image foundation model aiming at state-of-the-art quality and prompt following with commercial use.

license.name: MIT (transformer); text encoders carry their own licenses
license.notes: MIT License text (Copyright 2025 HiDream.ai) read in the HiDream-I1 GitHub repo LICENSE. Required text encoder Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct is under the Llama community license, which is a separate obligation.

architecture.kind: sparse diffusion transformer (MoE per paper title)

pc-16gb.notes: quant and offload No consumer-GPU seconds-per-image figure found in searches on 2026-11-19.

engine_support.notes: Not listed in the stable-diffusion.cpp README on 2026-11-15.

weaknesses: older (2025-04), below Nucleus-Image on the same benchmarks (vendor numbers)

tona_fit.reason: MIT weights and a strong 2025 GenEval/DPG score, but 17B plus an 8B Llama encoder makes it a quantized-only fit at 16 GB and the 2026 small models (Z-Image Turbo, FLUX.2 klein) reach similar quality at a fraction of the size.
blockers: needs Llama-3.1-8B encoder under a second license

sources.note: our research note 52, facts fetched 2026-11-15, not a measurement
MIT text, read through a summarizer

open_questions: VRAM and step counts not on the card
